topic: There is nothing to write and nobody to impress
text:
Swedish admission to most programmes is a number. You establish eligibility, you are given a merit value from your school results, and places go down the ranking. No motivation letter, no interview, no reference, no portfolio outside the arts schools.

Students coming from an internationally-minded school often find this disorienting, because the effort they have been taught to put into presenting themselves has nowhere to go. The useful consequence is the opposite of discouraging: nothing about the application can be got wrong through inexperience, and nothing about it rewards polish. What is left is ranking your choices honestly, and that genuinely matters — you receive at most one offer, the highest-ranked place that accepts you.
attribution: The national admissions authority’s description of how selection and ranking work
